references.text: The Lord reveals himself to Moses as a merciful and gracious God who keeps steadfast love for a thousand generations—the same description of God's mercy found in Deuteronomy 4:31
The Lord is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love—affirming God's merciful nature
Moses assures the people that the Lord will not let them go or forsake them—the same promise that God will not abandon his people
The Lord goes before you and will not let you go or forsake you—reiterating the promise of God's faithfulness
God promises Joshua that he will not let him go or forsake him—a continuation of the promise from Deuteronomy
God promises to remember his covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham—God does not forget his covenant with the fathers
God makes a covenant with Noah and promises to remember it—God's faithfulness to his covenant promises
God heard Israel's groaning and remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—an example that God does not forget his covenant
Nehemiah confesses that God is gracious and merciful and did not forsake his people—a direct reference to God's mercy
The Lord is a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness—praise of God's mercy
The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love—a description of God's merciful character
God promises that he will never let us go or forsake us—a New Testament confirmation of the promise in Deuteronomy
